text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Intepreting Maastricht treaty would allow heads of state to postpone the third phase of European monetary and economic union (EMU) now set to begin in 1999, European justice professor Kari Joutsamo at University of Helsinki says.
- Tax increase on public transport, which finance ministry plans, becomes costly to municipalities and travellers, Finnish bus alliance says.
- Heat wave lasting weeks has aggravated thick blooms of toxic blue-green algae in Finnish lakes all around the country.
KAUPPALEHTI
- No major tax cuts can be promised before state stops running a budget deficit, planned for 2001, finance ministry says.
- Finnish financial market supervision in banking and insurance needs major restructuring, system's incoherence is a vast problem, says Bjorn Wahlroos, appointed by finance ministry to study system.

- International phone calls in EU region will be reduced by 40-60 percent in coming years as European Commission liberalisation of markets, Timo Lahteenmaki at Finnish regional tele operator Finnet says.
- Exclusive apartments and houses have become scarce in Helsinki amid sharp upturn in demand, property representatives say.
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish know-how in log-house building has increased export markets to Asian countries, but competition between exporters may cut prices too far, sector representatives fear.
- Gains on medicine tax cuts will all go into consumers' pockets; medicine costs will fall by about 40 markka yearly, pharmaceutical sector says.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Customs officials investigate Swedish dairy Carlsham Mejeri Ab, which is owned by Finnish food group Raisio .
- State's continuing stringent budget policy satisfies Finnish economists: current growth would not allow any other kind of rational economic policy, they say.
- Nature healers' methods of treating illnesses are effective, Finnish medical study shows.
- Oldest Finnish film production company Fiminor, founded in 1962, declared bankrupt.
DEMARI
- MP Pertti Virtanen, the ecological party's only MP, says he is undecided on whether to run in next presidential and parliament elections.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Growing Internet use in stockbroking has opened new opportunities, but it may also lead to volatility through information overload, analyst Hannu Angervuo says.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
